title: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

title: CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT FACILITY EOAFRICA+
description: EO AFRICA+ is a 36-month capacity development facility designed to strengthen sustainable African capabilities in Earth Observation(EO) science, applications and innovation. Building on the achievements and community established through the EO AFRICA RD Facility, the activity will support African researchers, educators, institutions and early-career professionals in independently adopting, developing and applying EO technologies to address priority challenges across the continent.The facility combines curriculum development and Training of Trainers with a broad programme of face-to-face and online training, webinars, validation and field activities, and innovation challenges. It will strengthen the integration of EO into African higher education through reusable multilingual training materials and Africa-led training kits, while promoting practical learning and institutional uptake. Training will be supported by an open-source Training Management System and dedicated EO computing environments.EO AFRICA+ will foster African-European scientific cooperation through competitive Tandem RD Projects addressing priority African research challenges. The projects will combine skills transfer with access to advanced EO data, computing and open-science tools, producing reusable methods, software, datasetsand scientific outputs.A dedicated platform, implemented using ESA APEx, will provide the technical environment for practical training, research and prototyping. EO AFRICA+ will further strengthen the African EO community through outreach, an Advisory Board and broader community engagement, while supporting the long-term sustainability, reuse and African ownership of the capacities, knowledge and resources developed.

title: PHASE A SAMPLING THE NEUTRAL DENSITY OF THE LOWER THERMOSPHERE - EXPRO+
description: Objectives and TasksThe activity aims to reach a preliminary design for a dedicated mission that will measure in-situ the neutral density, and when feasible the ion density as well, in very low-Earth orbit, i.e. the lower thermosphere below 250km and if feasiblebelow 200km, from aneccentric orbit with high inclination. The eccentricity shall be tuned to ensure orbital lifetimes spanning a significant part of the solar cycle and the high inclination shall ensure the capture of samples across the dynamic atmospheric regions that affect the majority of current spacecraft and can support the new generation of VLEO satellites.To couple in-situ measurements that can be used to calibrate atmosphere models in the region of interest with space safety applications such as improved orbital lifetime estimation of collision avoidance risk assessment, direct coupling with the mission dragprofiles is needed. Therefore, the mission shall embark an accelerometer and optimise its shape and AOCS control to facilitate precise orbit determination.Very low perigee orbits, with apogee still in low Earth orbit, are a challenge for space surveillance and tracking systems due to limited visibility from individual sensors and the orbit being highly affected by drag. The mission shall function as a calibration target for commercial tracking solution in Europe, to demonstrate the accuracy of their products against a ground truth provide by the mission in support of safely operating in the VLEO regime.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, the orbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need of performing orbital lifetime calculation and collision avoidance processes below 300km. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed. This includes the basiclayout of the satellite, the platform mass and size, the orbit, the major components and subsystems considering as well launch vehicle, and groundsegment. Definition of the payload (e.g. mass spectrometers, accelerometers). Identify all critical items (< TRL 6) and derive technology development plans for each including definition of the VV approach. Given the eccentric orbit crossing highly utilised space traffic reason, perform a trade-off in platform manoeuvrability needs to extend the mission duration while managing collusion risk in accordance with ESA's space debris mitigation requirements. Preliminary cost and schedule: estimate of costs and schedules is developed based on the conceptual design, and the system requirements to be below 25MEUR. Risk assessment: risks associated with the mission and satellite design will be identified, evaluated, and assessed. Feasibility analysis: the feasibility of the mission and satellite design is assessed, taking into account technical, cost, and schedule considerations. Analysis of the commercialisation opportunities related to the mission concept and the related technologies.
